solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, enumeration length, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's answer wrong at 28 across, corrected here

clue.text: Misplaced director given support by constituency club

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
an MP's seat is the constituency they represent
a driver is a golf club for long tee shots

explanation.surface: A film director who has lost his job is backed by a local party club.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is wry: a passenger who directs the driver from behind is a director in the wrong place.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a passenger who keeps giving unwanted instructions to whoever is at the wheel, directing from the wrong seat.

clue.text: Dancing's no good in reel

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letter for good is dropped

parts.note: bobbing up and down is a kind of dancing; the 's is just 'is'

explanation.surface: A remark that someone's dancing in a Scottish reel is poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reel' reads as a Scottish dance, matching 'Dancing'; it is really a spool for thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel and a bobbin are both spools onto which thread or yarn is wound.

clue.text: Give credit to ordinary seaman, nearly half asleep on rising, for attempting this?

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
nearly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: someone drowsy is half asleep

explanation.surface: Praise a sailor who is dozing as he gets up for having a go at this puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' points to the very puzzle being solved, so the clue praises the solver as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's 'this' refers to the puzzle grid the solver is attempting, a word game of interlocking answers.

clue.text: Secrecy achieved by athletes painfully giving up drug

indicators.note: painfully suggests the letters of athletes being contorted into a new order
giving up shows the drug's letter is surrendered from the mix

parts.note: the word athletes supplies the pool of letters to be reshuffled
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Doping is kept secret when athletes in pain give up a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painfully' rearranges ATHLETES, and 'giving up' drops one E (ecstasy) from that pool, leaving the seven letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is acting covertly so as not to be noticed, which is a form of secrecy.

clue.text: In 'A Taste of Newquay' girl's swallowed pasty

indicators.note: the girl has been swallowed, so her pronoun goes inside the other letters
a taste is a small sample, here just the first letter

parts.note: she is a pronoun standing for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl on holiday in Cornwall eats a Cornish pasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like the Cornish pie, fitting Newquay (a Cornish seaside town), but it is the adjective meaning pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasty as an adjective describes a pale, unhealthy complexion, which is what an ashen face looks like.

clue.text: See 1 across
Knock up cassoulet at a tarty gathering

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters run from bottom to top, backwards
the answer's letters are gathered together inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A rowdy party where guests are served cassoulet, an image of a loud knock on the door.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cassoulet AT A TARty backwards to get the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated word imitates the sound of repeated rapping, so it is a knock.

clue.text: Dvorak's writing effaced when overturning drink …

indicators.note: effaced shows a letter is rubbed out of the name
overturning means the composer's name is upset and its letters rearranged

parts.note: Dvorak is the Czech composer's surname, which supplies the letter pool; the 's is a link
writing is one of the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: A composer's manuscripts are lost when someone knocks over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'effaced' removes R (writing, one of the three Rs) from DVORAK, and 'overturning' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Vodka is a clear spirit, a common alcoholic drink.

clue.text: … he liked a Bourbon in solitary state

indicators.note: in and state together say the word is in a state, so jumbled
being in a state means disordered, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A man who enjoyed his whiskey alone, following the drink in the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bourbon' follows the vodka clue so it looks like whiskey; here it is the French royal house.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the monarchy, such as one backing the Bourbon kings of France, is a monarchist.

clue.text: War-torn city in Cambodia with a port more than half destroyed

parts.note: K is the international vehicle registration for Cambodia
and means together with

indicators.note: four of the seven letters are removed, more than half

parts.note: a harbour is a port

explanation.surface: A ruined Asian port described in a war report.
explanation.definitionFit: Kandahar in Afghanistan saw heavy fighting in recent wars, so it is a city torn by war.

clue.text: Gone wrong? Listen to Edward — fifty years in a depressed state

parts.note: something broken has gone wrong
to hear is to listen to
Ted is a short form of Edward
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A man named Edward hears, at fifty, that things went wrong and he is low.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with a heavy heart after grief or disappointment is the same as acting in a depressed state.

clue.text: Nun is ill, sadly, lacking element of luteinizing hormone

indicators.note: sadly suggests the nun's words have gone wrong and are jumbled
lacking shows that letter is taken from the jumbled pool

parts.note: these three words supply the pool of letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: an element is a part, here the opening letter

explanation.surface: An ill nun is short of a component of a fertility hormone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges NUN IS ILL and 'lacking' removes L, the first letter of 'luteinizing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the pancreatic hormone that regulates blood sugar.

clue.text: Girl attending dance where no-one scores

parts.note: Dot is a girl's name, short for Dorothy
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A girl at a dance where nobody pairs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scores' suggests romance at the dance; in cricket a dot ball is a delivery off which no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a delivery from which the batter makes no run is recorded as a dot on the scoresheet.

clue.text: Bear repeated ridicule?

indicators.note: repeated means the bear's name is given twice

parts.note: Pooh is Winnie-the-Pooh, the bear of A A Milne's stories

explanation.surface: A bear being mocked over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss something scornfully as worthless is to ridicule it.

clue.text: Might this be Donna at times?

parts.note: the words on and, with off as an anagram signal, rearrange into the name Donna

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a woman called Donna comes and goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: the letters ON AND, sent 'off', make DONNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something intermittently, now and then, is doing it at times.

clue.text: Wraps coats around …

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wraps coats round themselves, leading into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacos are folded tortillas wrapped around a filling, so they are wraps.

clue.text: Scoundrel's tax certain to be topped — it's not on the level!

parts.note: a cur is a scoundrel; the 's links him to the tax
VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax

indicators.note: topped means having its head cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A rogue's tax claim is certain to be cut off, as it is crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on the level' reads as dishonest; it really means not flat, i.e. bent.
explanation.definitionFit: Curvature is the state of being curved, so anything with it is not flat or level.

clue.text: Fed not involved — put in cross-border cops

indicators.note: not involved means the word for fed plays no part, so it is removed

parts.note: to interpolate is to put in or insert
ate means fed, as in dined

explanation.surface: An American federal agent stays out of it, and the international police are brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed' looks like an FBI agent, fitting the police theme, but it is ATE, past tense of eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpol is the international organisation coordinating police across national borders.

clue.text: … models employed by non-U designer

indicators.note: the answer is employed within the run of words non-U designer

explanation.surface: A designer lacking social class hires models who wear nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U means not upper class, a British social label.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists' models who pose without clothes are nudes.

clue.text: Way 'e's taken to quicker 25ac

indicators.note: the letter written as 'e is taken away from the word

parts.note: a street is a way or road
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cockney instruction on which way to go, leading to a faster piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'e is Cockney for 'he' but here is just the letter E removed from STREET. 25ac refers to PASSAGE: a stretto is a fast closing passage in music.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a stretto is a section, often at the end, played at increased speed.

clue.text: 'Arsh-sounding verb 'to listen' (in Cockney) still among Chambers' top words!

indicators.note: sounding tells us the letters spell the way the word is spoken

parts.note: a Cockney's 'arsh is harsh, and the synonym hard is said 'ard
V is the abbreviation for verb in dictionaries

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops the initial H

parts.note: hark means to listen

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry in Cockney dialect is still near the top of the list.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers is a British dictionary; the animal's name is still among its first entries.
explanation.definitionFit: This African anteater's name is the first or near-first headword in most English dictionaries, including Chambers.

clue.text: Poetical evenings with ghastly verse (including spelling)

indicators.note: including means the spelling letters go inside
ghastly verse is bad verse, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Poetry evenings where verse is terrible, spelling and all.
explanation.definitionFit: Vesper is a poetic word for evening, so its plural serves as poetical evenings; it is also evening prayer.

clue.text: Put down and imprisoned

definitions.meaning: to put something down in writing is to write it
animals are ... in an enclosure, shut in

explanation.definitionFit: Writing words with a pen is putting them down; shutting animals in a fold is confining them.

clue.text: Rebounded, having suffered with loss of smell, and carried on

indicators.note: the word Rebounded has suffered damage, so its letters are jumbled
with loss of shows those letters are taken out of the pool

parts.note: the word Rebounded supplies the pool of letters to be rearranged
BO is body odour, a smell

explanation.surface: Someone who bounced back after losing their sense of smell, and kept going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having suffered' rearranges REBOUNDED and 'with loss of' removes BO (body odour, from 'smell').
explanation.definitionFit: To have persisted or kept going despite difficulty is to have carried on.

clue.text: Spirit seen and heard?

parts.note: a spirit seen is a genie of Arab legend; the same sounds like a spirit drink

explanation.definitionFit: A genie is a supernatural spirit of Islamic lore, and its name sounds like the juniper spirit.

clue.text: Lobby publicity agents? Wise man

parts.note: PAs are press agents, who handle publicity
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: Lobby groups of spin doctors consult a wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobby is a hall or corridor, the same as a passageway leading between rooms.

clue.text: Pardon me, OK? Not even for a push

indicators.note: not even means take the odd letters, first, third and so on

explanation.surface: Someone excusing themselves as they shove past.
explanation.definitionFit: A promo is a promotion, a publicity push for a product.

clue.text: Where advance is inevitable on Fot Niop?

parts.note: the made-up name is the words point of written backwards, so the answer is read as a joking instruction about them

explanation.surface: A puzzling place name, perhaps a spot on a map where an army can only push forward.
explanation.walkthrough: FOT NIOP is POINT OF written backwards: those words did turn back, the joke being that the answer forbids exactly that. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage beyond which turning back is impossible, so carrying on is the only option.

clue.text: Bird's catching no good for a fielder

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the bird wraps the other letters

parts.note: a loon is a diving bird, the North American name for a diver

explanation.surface: A bird that catches poorly is a useless fielder in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: Long on is a cricket fielding position deep on the leg side behind the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Long on names a cricket fielding position, and so the player stationed there.

clue.text: Convenience needs refurbishing — one of Clive Anderson's?

parts.note: a loo is a toilet, a public convenience

indicators.note: refurbishing means the letters are done up in a new order

explanation.surface: A public toilet needs doing up, as a broadcaster might say.
explanation.walkthrough: Clive Anderson presents Loose Ends, a BBC Radio 4 chat show, so one unfinished detail is one of his.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfinished detail is a loose end, and the broadcaster hosts a radio show called Loose Ends.
